about: Every JVM instruction javap prints, with a plain-English description. The opcodes, operands and stack behaviour are in src/core/jvm/opcodes.ts; the text is here. The wide forms are named as javap names them (iload_w).

source.spec: The Java Virtual Machine Specification, Java SE 25 Edition, chapter 6 (The Java Virtual Machine Instruction Set)
source.text: Descriptions written for this project; follow the links for the authoritative text

aaload.summary: Load a reference from an array
aaload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the reference element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

aastore.summary: Store a reference into an array
aastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. Throws ArrayStoreException when the object's class does not fit the array's element type. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

aload.description: Pushes a reference from the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode. Parameters are the first locals: this (in an instance method) is slot 0.

aload_0.description: Pushes a reference from local variable 0. One byte in place of aload 0. In an instance method local 0 is this.

aload_1.description: Pushes a reference from local variable 1. One byte in place of aload 1.

aload_2.description: Pushes a reference from local variable 2. One byte in place of aload 2.

aload_3.description: Pushes a reference from local variable 3. One byte in place of aload 3.

aload_w.description: Pushes a reference from a local variable, as aload does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

anewarray.description: Pops a length and pushes a new array of that many null references, of the class, interface or array type named.

areturn.description: Pops a reference and returns it to the caller, whose stack gets it. In a synchronized method the monitor is released first.

arraylength.description: Pops an array and pushes its length. Throws NullPointerException on null.

astore.description: Pops a reference and stores it in the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode. astore also stores the return address jsr pushes.

astore_0.description: Pops a reference and stores it in local variable 0. One byte in place of astore 0.

astore_1.description: Pops a reference and stores it in local variable 1. One byte in place of astore 1.

astore_2.description: Pops a reference and stores it in local variable 2. One byte in place of astore 2.

astore_3.description: Pops a reference and stores it in local variable 3. One byte in place of astore 3.

astore_w.description: Pops a reference and stores it in a local variable, as astore does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

athrow.description: Pops a Throwable and throws it: the nearest handler of the method that covers this instruction and catches its class gets it on an empty stack; if none does, the method ends and the caller's handlers are looked at. Throws NullPointerException on null.

baload.summary: Load a byte or boolean from an array
baload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the byte or boolean element at that index. The byte is sign-extended to an int (a boolean array holds 0 and 1). Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

bastore.summary: Store a byte or boolean into an array
bastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. The int is truncated to its low 8 bits (for a boolean array, its lowest bit). Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

bipush.description: Pushes the signed byte that follows the opcode, sign-extended to an int: constants from -128 to 127.

caload.summary: Load a char from an array
caload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the char element at that index. The char is zero-extended to an int. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

castore.summary: Store a char into an array
castore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. The int is truncated to its low 16 bits. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

checkcast.description: Pops a reference and pushes it back unchanged if it is null or an instance of the type named; otherwise throws ClassCastException: (Type) x.

d2f.description: Pops double and pushes it as float. Rounds the double to the nearest float; too large becomes an infinity, too small zero.

d2i.description: Pops double and pushes it as int. Drops the fraction (rounds toward zero). A NaN gives 0, and a value outside the int range gives Integer.MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE.

d2l.description: Pops double and pushes it as long. Drops the fraction; a NaN gives 0, a value outside the long range Long.MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE.

dadd.description: Pops two doubles and pushes their sum. IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounding to nearest.

daload.summary: Load a double from an array
daload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the double element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

dastore.summary: Store a double into an array
dastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

dcmpg.description: Pops b, then a, two doubles, and pushes 1 if a > b, 0 if they are equal and -1 if a < b — and 1 when either is NaN. javac picks it for < and <= tests, so that a NaN makes them false.

dcmpl.description: Pops b, then a, two doubles, and pushes 1 if a > b, 0 if they are equal and -1 if a < b — and -1 when either is NaN. javac picks it for > and >= tests, so that a NaN makes them false.

ddiv.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a / b by IEEE 754: dividing by zero gives an infinity or NaN, never an exception.

dload.description: Pushes a double (two slots) from the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode. Parameters are the first locals: this (in an instance method) is slot 0.

dload_0.description: Pushes a double (two slots) from local variable 0. One byte in place of dload 0.

dload_1.description: Pushes a double (two slots) from local variable 1. One byte in place of dload 1.

dload_2.description: Pushes a double (two slots) from local variable 2. One byte in place of dload 2.

dload_3.description: Pushes a double (two slots) from local variable 3. One byte in place of dload 3.

dload_w.description: Pushes a double (two slots) from a local variable, as dload does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

dmul.description: Pops two doubles and pushes their product. IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounding to nearest.

dneg.description: Pops a value and pushes its negation. Flips the sign bit: -0.0 and 0.0 trade places, NaN stays NaN.

drem.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes the remainder of a / b with the quotient truncated toward zero, as C's fmod — not IEEE 754's remainder (that is Math.IEEEremainder). It has the sign of a.

dreturn.description: Pops a double and returns it to the caller, whose stack gets it. In a synchronized method the monitor is released first.

dstore.description: Pops a double (two slots) and stores it in the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode.

dstore_0.description: Pops a double (two slots) and stores it in local variable 0. One byte in place of dstore 0.

dstore_1.description: Pops a double (two slots) and stores it in local variable 1. One byte in place of dstore 1.

dstore_2.description: Pops a double (two slots) and stores it in local variable 2. One byte in place of dstore 2.

dstore_3.description: Pops a double (two slots) and stores it in local variable 3. One byte in place of dstore 3.

dstore_w.description: Pops a double (two slots) and stores it in a local variable, as dstore does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

dsub.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a − b. IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounding to nearest.

dup.description: Pushes a copy of the one-slot value on top. javac uses it for new (the object for the constructor and the one kept), for x = y = z, and for x++ on fields.

dup2.description: Pushes a copy of the top two slots: one long or double, or two one-slot values (an array and an index for a[i]++, say).
dup2.operation: b a → b a b a

dup2_x1.summary: Duplicate two slots under the next
dup2_x1.description: Copies the top two slots (a long or double, or two values) and inserts the copy below the one-slot value under them.
dup2_x1.operation: c b a → b a c b a

dup2_x2.summary: Duplicate two slots under the next two
dup2_x2.description: Copies the top two slots and inserts the copy two slots further down; each pair may be one long or double or two one-slot values.
dup2_x2.operation: d c b a → b a d c b a

dup_x1.summary: Duplicate the top value under the next
dup_x1.description: Copies the one-slot value on top and inserts the copy below the value under it: an assignment to a field used as a value, obj.f = v, needs it.

dup_x2.summary: Duplicate the top value under the next two slots
dup_x2.description: Copies the one-slot value on top and inserts the copy two slots down: below two one-slot values, or below one long or double. Used for an assignment to an array element used as a value.
dup_x2.operation: c b a → a c b a

f2d.description: Pops float and pushes it as double. Widens the float to a double, exactly.

f2i.description: Pops float and pushes it as int. Drops the fraction (rounds toward zero). A NaN gives 0, and a value outside the int range gives Integer.MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE: Java saturates, it does not wrap.

f2l.description: Pops float and pushes it as long. Drops the fraction; a NaN gives 0, a value outside the long range Long.MIN_VALUE or MAX_VALUE.

fadd.description: Pops two floats and pushes their sum. IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounding to nearest.

faload.summary: Load a float from an array
faload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the float element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

fastore.summary: Store a float into an array
fastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

fcmpg.description: Pops b, then a, two floats, and pushes 1 if a > b, 0 if they are equal and -1 if a < b — and 1 when either is NaN. javac picks it for < and <= tests, so that a NaN makes them false.

fcmpl.description: Pops b, then a, two floats, and pushes 1 if a > b, 0 if they are equal and -1 if a < b — and -1 when either is NaN. javac picks it for > and >= tests, so that a NaN makes them false.

fdiv.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a / b by IEEE 754: dividing by zero gives an infinity or NaN, never an exception.

fload.description: Pushes a float from the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode. Parameters are the first locals: this (in an instance method) is slot 0.

fload_0.description: Pushes a float from local variable 0. One byte in place of fload 0.

fload_1.description: Pushes a float from local variable 1. One byte in place of fload 1.

fload_2.description: Pushes a float from local variable 2. One byte in place of fload 2.

fload_3.description: Pushes a float from local variable 3. One byte in place of fload 3.

fload_w.description: Pushes a float from a local variable, as fload does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

fmul.description: Pops two floats and pushes their product. IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounding to nearest.

fneg.description: Pops a value and pushes its negation. Flips the sign bit: -0.0 and 0.0 trade places, NaN stays NaN.

frem.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes the remainder of a / b with the quotient truncated toward zero, as C's fmod — not IEEE 754's remainder (that is Math.IEEEremainder). It has the sign of a.

freturn.description: Pops a float and returns it to the caller, whose stack gets it. In a synchronized method the monitor is released first.

fstore.description: Pops a float and stores it in the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode.

fstore_0.description: Pops a float and stores it in local variable 0. One byte in place of fstore 0.

fstore_1.description: Pops a float and stores it in local variable 1. One byte in place of fstore 1.

fstore_2.description: Pops a float and stores it in local variable 2. One byte in place of fstore 2.

fstore_3.description: Pops a float and stores it in local variable 3. One byte in place of fstore 3.

fstore_w.description: Pops a float and stores it in a local variable, as fstore does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

fsub.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a − b. IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounding to nearest.

getfield.summary: Read a field of an object
getfield.description: Pops an object and pushes the value of its field (a Fieldref). Throws NullPointerException on null.

getstatic.description: Pushes the value of a class's static field, named by a Fieldref in the constant pool. The class is initialized first if it has not been.

goto.description: Goes to the target, a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction: the jump back of a loop, the jump past an else.

goto_w.description: Goes to the target, a signed 32-bit offset from this instruction. A method's code is under 64 KiB, so compilers hardly need it.

i2b.description: Pops int and pushes it as byte. Keeps the low 8 bits of the int and sign-extends them back to an int: (byte) x.

i2c.description: Pops int and pushes it as char. Keeps the low 16 bits of the int and zero-extends them back to an int: (char) x.

i2d.description: Pops int and pushes it as double. Converts the int to a double, exactly.

i2f.description: Pops int and pushes it as float. Converts the int to the nearest float; a large int may lose its low digits.

i2l.description: Pops int and pushes it as long. Sign-extends the int to a long; nothing is lost.

i2s.description: Pops int and pushes it as short. Keeps the low 16 bits of the int and sign-extends them back to an int: (short) x.

iadd.description: Pops two ints and pushes their sum. On overflow it wraps around (only the low bits are kept); Math.addExact is the checked form.

iaload.summary: Load a int from an array
iaload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the int element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

iand.description: Pops two ints and pushes their bitwise AND: Java's & on integers, and on booleans when both sides must be evaluated.

iastore.summary: Store a int into an array
iastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

iconst_0.description: Pushes the int constant 0. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

iconst_1.description: Pushes the int constant 1. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

iconst_2.description: Pushes the int constant 2. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

iconst_3.description: Pushes the int constant 3. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

iconst_4.description: Pushes the int constant 4. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

iconst_5.description: Pushes the int constant 5. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

iconst_m1.description: Pushes the int constant -1. One byte in place of bipush for the most common small numbers.

idiv.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a / b rounded toward zero. Throws ArithmeticException when b is 0; the smallest int divided by -1 gives itself.

if_acmpeq.summary: Branch if references are the same
if_acmpeq.description: Pops two references and goes to the target if they are the same object (or both null): Java's == on objects, not equals().

if_acmpne.description: Pops two references and goes to the target if they are not the same object.

if_icmpeq.description: Pops b, then a, two ints, and goes to the target if they are equal; otherwise the next instruction runs.

if_icmpge.description: Pops b, then a, two ints, and goes to the target if a >= b; otherwise the next instruction runs.

if_icmpgt.description: Pops b, then a, two ints, and goes to the target if a > b; otherwise the next instruction runs.

if_icmple.description: Pops b, then a, two ints, and goes to the target if a <= b; otherwise the next instruction runs.

if_icmplt.description: Pops b, then a, two ints, and goes to the target if a < b; otherwise the next instruction runs.

if_icmpne.summary: Branch if ints are not equal
if_icmpne.description: Pops b, then a, two ints, and goes to the target if they are not equal; otherwise the next instruction runs.

ifeq.summary: Branch if int is equal to zero
ifeq.description: Pops an int and goes to the target (a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction) if it is equal to zero; otherwise the next instruction runs. After a comparison (lcmp, fcmpl…) it tests the comparison; on a boolean, ifeq means false and ifne true.

ifge.summary: Branch if int is zero or more
ifge.description: Pops an int and goes to the target (a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction) if it is zero or more; otherwise the next instruction runs. After lcmp, fcmpl or dcmpg it tests the comparison.

ifgt.summary: Branch if int is greater than zero
ifgt.description: Pops an int and goes to the target (a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction) if it is greater than zero; otherwise the next instruction runs. After lcmp, fcmpl or dcmpg it tests the comparison.

ifle.summary: Branch if int is zero or less
ifle.description: Pops an int and goes to the target (a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction) if it is zero or less; otherwise the next instruction runs. After lcmp, fcmpl or dcmpg it tests the comparison.

iflt.summary: Branch if int is less than zero
iflt.description: Pops an int and goes to the target (a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction) if it is less than zero; otherwise the next instruction runs. After lcmp, fcmpl or dcmpg it tests the comparison.

ifne.summary: Branch if int is not zero
ifne.description: Pops an int and goes to the target (a signed 16-bit offset from this instruction) if it is not zero; otherwise the next instruction runs. After a comparison (lcmp, fcmpl…) it tests the comparison; on a boolean, ifeq means false and ifne true.

ifnonnull.description: Pops a reference and goes to the target if it is not null.

ifnull.description: Pops a reference and goes to the target if it is null.

iinc.description: Adds the signed byte that follows the slot number to the int in that local variable, without touching the stack: i++, i += 5, i -= 1.

iinc_w.description: Adds a signed 16-bit constant to the int in a local variable, as iinc does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes both the slot number and the constant two bytes.

iload.description: Pushes an int from the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode. Parameters are the first locals: this (in an instance method) is slot 0.

iload_0.description: Pushes an int from local variable 0. One byte in place of iload 0.

iload_1.description: Pushes an int from local variable 1. One byte in place of iload 1.

iload_2.description: Pushes an int from local variable 2. One byte in place of iload 2.

iload_3.description: Pushes an int from local variable 3. One byte in place of iload 3.

iload_w.description: Pushes an int from a local variable, as iload does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

imul.description: Pops two ints and pushes their product. On overflow it wraps around (only the low bits are kept); Math.multiplyExact is the checked form.

ineg.description: Pops a value and pushes its negation. The smallest int stays itself.

instanceof.summary: Test the type of an object
instanceof.description: Pops a reference and pushes 1 if it is an instance of the type named, 0 if not or if it is null: x instanceof Type.

invokedynamic.description: Pops the arguments and calls whatever the call site is linked to. The first time it runs, the bootstrap method the constant names builds the call site; javac uses it for lambdas and method references (LambdaMetafactory), string concatenation (StringConcatFactory), records' equals, hashCode and toString, and pattern switches.

invokeinterface.summary: Call a method of an interface
invokeinterface.description: Pops the arguments and the object and calls the object's implementation of an interface method. Its operands also give the number of argument slots (with the object) and a zero, which javap prints after the index.

invokespecial.description: Pops the arguments and the object and calls the very method named, without looking for an override: a constructor (<init>), a super.method() call, and in old class files private methods.

invokestatic.description: Pops the arguments and calls a static method; its result, if any, is pushed. The class is initialized first if it has not been.

invokevirtual.summary: Call a method of an object
invokevirtual.description: Pops the arguments and the object and calls the method the object's own class has for the name and descriptor — an override if there is one. The result, if any, is pushed. Throws NullPointerException on null.

ior.description: Pops two ints and pushes their bitwise OR: Java's |.

irem.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes the remainder of a / b, a − (a / b) × b: it has the sign of a. Throws ArithmeticException when b is 0.

ireturn.description: Pops an int (or a boolean, byte, char, short) and returns it to the caller, whose stack gets it. In a synchronized method the monitor is released first.

ishl.description: Pops a shift count (an int) and a value and pushes the value shifted left. Only the low 5 bits of the count are used, so it is taken modulo 32.

ishr.summary: Shift int right, keeping the sign
ishr.description: Pops a shift count (an int) and a value and pushes the value shifted right, copies of the sign bit filling in from the left: Java's >>. The count is taken modulo 32.

istore.description: Pops an int and stores it in the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode.

istore_0.description: Pops an int and stores it in local variable 0. One byte in place of istore 0.

istore_1.description: Pops an int and stores it in local variable 1. One byte in place of istore 1.

istore_2.description: Pops an int and stores it in local variable 2. One byte in place of istore 2.

istore_3.description: Pops an int and stores it in local variable 3. One byte in place of istore 3.

istore_w.description: Pops an int and stores it in a local variable, as istore does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

isub.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a − b. On overflow it wraps around (only the low bits are kept); Math.subtractExact is the checked form.

iushr.summary: Shift int right, filling with zeros
iushr.description: Pops a shift count (an int) and a value and pushes the value shifted right, zeros filling in from the left: Java's >>>. The count is taken modulo 32.

ixor.description: Pops two ints and pushes their bitwise exclusive OR: Java's ^. With -1 it inverts every bit, which is how ~x compiles.

jsr.description: Pushes the address of the next instruction and goes to the target: how old compilers (Java 1.4 and earlier) ran a finally block from every exit. Class files of version 51 (Java 7) and later may not use it. javap does not print its target.

jsr_w.description: Like jsr, with a signed 32-bit offset.

l2d.description: Pops long and pushes it as double. Converts the long to the nearest double; above 2^53 the low digits may be lost.

l2f.description: Pops long and pushes it as float. Converts the long to the nearest float.

l2i.description: Pops long and pushes it as int. Keeps the low 32 bits of the long: the value may change and even its sign.

ladd.description: Pops two longs and pushes their sum. On overflow it wraps around (only the low bits are kept); Math.addExact is the checked form.

laload.summary: Load a long from an array
laload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the long element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

land.description: Pops two longs and pushes their bitwise AND: Java's & on integers, and on booleans when both sides must be evaluated.

lastore.summary: Store a long into an array
lastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

lcmp.description: Pops b, then a, two longs, and pushes 1 if a > b, 0 if they are equal and -1 if a < b. A branch on the result (ifge, iflt…) follows.

ldc.description: Pushes a constant from the class's constant pool, named by a one-byte index: an int, a float, a String, a class (its Class object), a method type, a method handle, or a dynamic constant made by its bootstrap method on first use.

ldc2_w.summary: Load a long or double constant
ldc2_w.description: Pushes a long or a double (or a dynamic constant of one of those types) from the constant pool, by a two-byte index. Such constants take two pool entries and two stack slots.

ldc_w.description: Like ldc, with a two-byte index, for constants past the first 256 entries of the pool.

ldiv.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a / b rounded toward zero. Throws ArithmeticException when b is 0; the smallest long divided by -1 gives itself.

lload.description: Pushes a long (two slots) from the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode. Parameters are the first locals: this (in an instance method) is slot 0.

lload_0.description: Pushes a long (two slots) from local variable 0. One byte in place of lload 0.

lload_1.description: Pushes a long (two slots) from local variable 1. One byte in place of lload 1.

lload_2.description: Pushes a long (two slots) from local variable 2. One byte in place of lload 2.

lload_3.description: Pushes a long (two slots) from local variable 3. One byte in place of lload 3.

lload_w.description: Pushes a long (two slots) from a local variable, as lload does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

lmul.description: Pops two longs and pushes their product. On overflow it wraps around (only the low bits are kept); Math.multiplyExact is the checked form.

lneg.description: Pops a value and pushes its negation. The smallest long stays itself.

lookupswitch.description: Pops an int and goes to the target of the key equal to it, or to the default when none is. The keys are sorted, so it can be searched; compilers use it for a sparse switch, and for a switch on strings (by hashCode).

lor.description: Pops two longs and pushes their bitwise OR: Java's |.

lrem.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes the remainder of a / b, a − (a / b) × b: it has the sign of a. Throws ArithmeticException when b is 0.

lreturn.description: Pops a long and returns it to the caller, whose stack gets it. In a synchronized method the monitor is released first.

lshl.description: Pops a shift count (an int) and a value and pushes the value shifted left. Only the low 6 bits of the count are used, so it is taken modulo 64.

lshr.summary: Shift long right, keeping the sign
lshr.description: Pops a shift count (an int) and a value and pushes the value shifted right, copies of the sign bit filling in from the left: Java's >>. The count is taken modulo 64.

lstore.description: Pops a long (two slots) and stores it in the local variable whose slot number follows the opcode.

lstore_0.description: Pops a long (two slots) and stores it in local variable 0. One byte in place of lstore 0.

lstore_1.description: Pops a long (two slots) and stores it in local variable 1. One byte in place of lstore 1.

lstore_2.description: Pops a long (two slots) and stores it in local variable 2. One byte in place of lstore 2.

lstore_3.description: Pops a long (two slots) and stores it in local variable 3. One byte in place of lstore 3.

lstore_w.description: Pops a long (two slots) and stores it in a local variable, as lstore does. Wide form: the wide prefix (0xC4) makes the slot number two bytes, so slots up to 65535 can be reached.

lsub.description: Pops b, then a, and pushes a − b. On overflow it wraps around (only the low bits are kept); Math.subtractExact is the checked form.

lushr.summary: Shift long right, filling with zeros
lushr.description: Pops a shift count (an int) and a value and pushes the value shifted right, zeros filling in from the left: Java's >>>. The count is taken modulo 64.

lxor.description: Pops two longs and pushes their bitwise exclusive OR: Java's ^. With -1 it inverts every bit, which is how ~x compiles.

monitorenter.description: Pops an object and takes its lock, waiting while another thread holds it; the thread that holds it may take it again. The start of a synchronized block. Throws NullPointerException on null.

monitorexit.description: Pops an object and releases one hold of its lock. javac puts it at every way out of a synchronized block, the exceptional one too.

multianewarray.description: Pops one length per dimension the operand gives and pushes a new array of the array type named, with its sub-arrays made: new int[3][4]. Dimensions past those given stay null: new String[2][].

new.description: Allocates an object of the class named and pushes a reference to it, its fields zero. It is not yet constructed: javac follows it with dup, the arguments and invokespecial <init>.

newarray.summary: Create an array of a primitive type
newarray.description: Pops a length and pushes a new array of that many elements of the primitive type named by the operand byte (boolean, char, float, double, byte, short, int or long), each zero. Throws NegativeArraySizeException for a negative length.

nop.description: Does nothing. Compilers rarely emit it; it can keep room in code that is patched later.

pop.description: Pops the value on top of the stack and throws it away: a call's result that is not used, say. The value must be one slot (not a long or a double).

pop2.description: Pops two slots and throws them away: one long or double, or two values of one slot each.

putfield.summary: Write a field of an object
putfield.description: Pops a value and an object and stores the value in the object's field (a Fieldref). Throws NullPointerException on null.

putstatic.description: Pops a value and stores it in a class's static field (a Fieldref). The class is initialized first if it has not been.

ret.description: Goes to the return address held in the local variable whose slot follows the opcode, where jsr's astore put it: the end of an old-style finally block. javap does not print the slot.

ret_w.description: Like ret, for a local variable past slot 255: the wide prefix makes the slot number two bytes.

return.description: Returns to the caller with no value: the end of a void method or constructor.

saload.summary: Load a short from an array
saload.description: Pops an index and an array and pushes the short element at that index. The short is sign-extended to an int. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

sastore.summary: Store a short into an array
sastore.description: Pops a value, an index and an array and stores the value as the element at that index. The int is truncated to its low 16 bits. Throws NullPointerException on a null array and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on an index outside it.

sipush.description: Pushes the signed 16-bit number that follows the opcode, sign-extended to an int: constants from -32768 to 32767.

swap.description: Exchanges the two one-slot values on top of the stack. javac seldom needs it; other compilers do.

tableswitch.description: Pops an int and, if it is between the table's low and high values, goes to the target for it; otherwise to the default. Compilers use it for a dense switch. Its operands start at a multiple of four bytes from the start of the code.
